148a70836c0523bf18f18d8ccd3e3378b3b6c463.reason: The source explicitly states that political scientists used methods like speeches, diaries, autobiographies, roll-call votes, cognitive maps, and participant observation to study elites, which aligns with the claim of reliance on manual methods with limited scalability.

b64f806ccff6bd2667c5c723c56e8f8c560eb7f4.claim: Recent work on fine-grained citation grounding demonstrates that LLMs can reliably anchor claims to specific source sentences when constrained to do so
b64f806ccff6bd2667c5c723c56e8f8c560eb7f4.reason: The source explicitly states that the work enables long-context LLMs to generate responses with fine-grained sentence-level citations, and the trained models achieve state-of-the-art citation quality, demonstrating that LLMs can reliably anchor claims to specific source sentences when constrained to do so.

06fd32dc951412ccca6d205c788989c2969a1eab.claim: (2023) demonstrate that hallucinated outputs are detectable through self-consistency: when an LLM is asked the same question multiple times, hallucinated answers tend to diverge and contradict each other, while factual answers remain consistent across samples
06fd32dc951412ccca6d205c788989c2969a1eab.reason: Phrases 6 and 7 directly state that if an LLM has knowledge of a concept, sampled responses are similar and contain consistent facts, while for hallucinated facts, sampled responses diverge and contradict one another, which exactly matches the claim.

b9dc3e0bd89f3ee5bafb3bf4f28b5d6fb7753c18.claim: (2022) show that LLMs are substantially better at evaluating their own outputs than at generating correct ones—they can detect errors in existing text at much higher rates than they can avoid producing errors during generation
b9dc3e0bd89f3ee5bafb3bf4f28b5d6fb7753c18.reason: The source explicitly states that "verification improves faster than generation quality in this context," directly supporting the claim that LLMs are substantially better at evaluating their own outputs than at generating correct ones.

5d92ffd08236b73f666add973fd292e5a8961b49.claim: LongCite (2024) provides direct evidence that LLMs can reliably anchor claims to specific source sentences when trained and prompted to do so
5d92ffd08236b73f666add973fd292e5a8961b49.reason: The source explicitly states that training with the LongCite-45k dataset enabled the models to generate accurate responses and fine-grained sentence-level citations in a single output, directly supporting the claim.

43591cb235a3d3bb57c5a5b5579719e7afd8004b.claim: But LLMs hallucinate---they generate plausible-sounding but factually incorrect claims
43591cb235a3d3bb57c5a5b5579719e7afd8004b.reason: The source explicitly states that NLG models often generate text that is nonsensical or unfaithful to the source input, and that researchers refer to this as hallucination, which directly matches the claim that LLMs generate plausible-sounding but factually incorrect claims.

eb7edcfbf9961b7cc5bd129cf32b7c352bd0d694.claim: When the model lacks grounding in external facts, this distribution can produce plausible-sounding but incorrect statements
eb7edcfbf9961b7cc5bd129cf32b7c352bd0d694.reason: The source states that hallucinated text "gives the impression of being fluent and natural despite being unfaithful" and "appears to be grounded in the real context provided, although it is actually hard to specify or verify the existence of such contexts," which directly matches the claim that when the model lacks grounding in external facts, the distribution can produce plausible-sounding but incorrect statements.
